item.title: py-ARGOS: A Python package for automatic, statistically principled discovery of ordinary differential equations from data
item.description: arXiv:2610.34458v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recovering the governing equations of a dynamical system from data is a central problem in data-driven science, yet the available Python tooling forces a compromise among automation, statistical rigor, and reliability. We present py-ARGOS, a Python package implementing two automatic algorithms, bootstrap ARGOS and Bayesian-ARGOS, behind a uniform interface. Both are statistically principled throughout: automated model selection reduces the candidate library, each coefficient is reported with a bootstrap confidence or Bayesian credible interval that quantifies its uncertainty, and a term is retained when this interval excludes zero. Built-in diagnostics additionally flag unreliable fits. On chaotic benchmark systems, the two algorithms improve on the SINDy family's identification performance.
item.dc:creator: Yuzheng Zhang, Rui Carvalho

item.title: Using RngStreams for Parallel Random Number Generation in C++ and R
item.description: arXiv:1403.7645v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The RngStreams software package provides one viable solution to the problem of creating separate random number streams for simulations in parallel processing environments. Techniques are presented for effectively using RngStreams with C++ programs that are parallelized via OpenMP or MPI. Ways to access the backbone generator from RngStreams in R through the parallel and rstream packages are also described. The ideas in the paper are illustrated with both a simple running example and a Monte Carlo integration application.
item.dc:creator: Andrew T. Karl, Randy Eubank, Jelena Milovanovic, Mark Reiser, Dennis Young

item.title: A New Test for Hamming-Weight Dependencies
item.description: arXiv:2108.13061v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We describe a new statistical test for pseudorandom number generators (PRNGs). Our test can find bias induced by dependencies among the Hamming weights of the outputs of a PRNG, even for PRNGs that pass state-of-the-art tests of the same kind from the literature, and in particular for generators based on $\mathbf F_2$-linear transformations such as the dSFMT, xoroshiro1024+, and WELL512a.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: ACM Transactions on Modeling and Computer Simulation, 32(3), 2022
item.dc:creator: David Blackman, Sebastiano Vigna
